name: Heather Violet
lede: Heather Violet is a deep purplish pink matched to the moorland shrub heather, with no close match anywhere in our painting archive.

sections.title: A plant word paired with violet
sections.body:
The color library records Heather Violet from RAL 4003, dated 1927 [1]. Its name joins [[heather]], a plant word, with [[violet]], and the library does not explain why the two were paired [1].

Measured in LCH terms it sits at lightness 55, chroma 52, hue 354 degrees, inside the ISCC-NBS "deep purplish pink" block, Munsell notation 5.0RP 5.4/12.0, a step between [[violet]] and [[pink]] [1]. The nearest named color in our library is [[mulberry|Mulberry]], about 5.2 units away by CIEDE2000, a visible difference [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive comes within CIEDE2000 4 of this color while covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That is a limit of our archive's holdings, not a claim about painting generally [2]. The RAL sample is a paint standard, not a pigment measurement, so the hex value is a screen approximation [1][2].

origin.named_after: pairs the heather plant with a violet modifier; the choice itself is undocumented
